To narrow down the sequence space for active site residues, we investigated the structure of active variants using protein structure models generated by AlphaFold. Full homodimeric structures of ApbHACS and DhcHACS were constructed using the ColabFold platform (Rohwerder et al., 2020), which showed a high pLDDT score (> 90) throughout the sequence except for the N-terminal and C-terminal regions. The structures were aligned with the crystal structure of oxalyl-CoA decarboxylase from Oxalobacter formigenes (OfOXC) in complex with formyl-CoA (PDB code: 2JI8) to understand the position and orientation of the two key ligands, thiamine diphosphate (TPP) and formyl-CoA, in the active site. The AlphaFold models of ApbHACS and DhcHACS exhibit high structural similarity with the OfOXC crystal structure with root- mean-square distance (RMSD) values of 1.185 Å and 0.981 Å for ApbHACS and DhcHACS, respectively. The catalytic site (where TPP and the formyl residue of formyl- CoA interface for catalysis with the carbonyl-containing compound) and the CoA binding site are both exposed to the solvent space, suggesting accurate orientation of the ligands docked onto the ApbHACS and DhcHACS structures. Between the two best variants from the first round, we selected DhcHACS for further engineering as it exhibited the highest catalytic efficiency towards both formaldehyde and formyl-CoA (Table 5). To identify key residues of DhcHACS responsible for catalytic function and substrate binding, we focused on three specific regions of the active site: the TPP binding, formyl-CoA binding, and C-terminal tail regions. Literature reports that the TPP binding region is critical for the catalytic activity of all HACSs and OXC family enzymes. Formyl-CoA binding would be important in determining the affinity toward formyl-CoA, which could affect the catalytic function of the enzyme as well. Lastly, the 38 C-terminal tail was found to be folding over the active site of HACSs and OXCs, forming a “covering loop” that plays an important role in determining the substrate chain length specificity. Subsequently, residues within 3.5 Å from TPP and formyl-CoA based on the ligands-bound AlphaFold structure of DhcHACS, as well as the conserved C-terminal residues from the active variants, were selected for analysis. In parallel, the sequence of all 29 first-round HACS variants (HACS-1-1 to 29) and known enzymes from the OXC-HACS family (i.e., HsHACS, RuHACS, EcOXC, OfOXC, and MeOXC) were aligned to analyze residues from the three regions. Most of the residues in the TPP binding region are fully conserved among HACS and OXC variants, as expected, but much less conserved residues are observed in the formyl-CoA binding and C-terminal regions.
